newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar weaker in pre-expiry spread sale.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar weaker in pre-expiry spread sale.

text.p: White sugar futures moved into negative territory as a mixed bag of sellers capped the opening strength of the March/May spread in the little time remaining before spot expiry.
March/May traded out to as wide as $6.50 in solid early activity but then contracted to under $5.00 amid interest from trade, broker and commission house players.
Traders said the spot strength seemed to have been capped and the spread was unlikely to return to the wide levels seen in late trading on Tuesday.
Overall volume was also boosted by some outright selling by one leading trade house along with against actuals trades.
"It's all being tidied up before expiry tomorrow...but in the last day of trading anything can happen," said one trader.
At 1255 GMT March was down $1.60 at $306.50 and May down by the same amount at $302.00. Volume was 2,348 lots, nearly all in the front two positions.
In physical news, Sri Lanka bought 12,500 tonnes of white sugar from Gill & Duffus at $336.90 per tonne. Specified delivery dates are March 15/April 5.
Paris positions were mixed in a total volume of 1,149 lots. March was up $1.40 at $308.00 and May down 40 cents at $302.20.
